reviews.one_line_contribution: The information-abundance effect is re-cast as a placement effect: putting retrieved episodes in the *student's* prompt during agent SFT suppresses what gets written into weights (monotone in dose k, absent for length-matched relevance-destroyed decoys, and predicted by a per-example delta-NLL the memory affords), whereas giving the same dose only to a *teacher* in on-policy reverse-KL distillation with an empty student prompt does not — so the two dose-response curves cross.
reviews.closest_prior_work: arXiv:2608.12218 (Information Abundance Paradox: Long-Context Training Undermines Parametric Knowledge, 2026-08-12, verified via s2cli `paper`, cit 2). It already owns every load-bearing component of the mechanism claim: longer training context reduces parametric encoding, increases contextual reliance, and has an intermediate optimum. What is left for this proposal is (a) a new data type (ALFWorld trajectories rather than documents), (b) a length-matched decoy control, (c) the student-vs-teacher placement contrast. That is an 'X also holds on Y, and here is where it stops' paper, and the field's tolerance for that depends entirely on (c) being surprising — see the objection. Second threat, arXiv:2603.18272 (Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience, 2026-03-18, verified, cit 5): its 'retrieval-aware fine-tuning' IS the student-side k>0 arm on agent experience. The proposal asserts it never evaluates retrieval-free and never varies the dose; I could verify the paper's existence and framing but NOT that assertion (abstract only, no section text — WebSearch unavailable this session). If 2603.18272 contains a no-retrieval eval or a k-ablation in an appendix, the student-side ladder is a delta on one of its ablations rather than a new result, and a reviewer with the PDF will check this first. Third, the on-policy self-distillation family — OPCD arXiv:2602.12275 (verified, cit 132) and OPSD 2601.18734 — already trains empty-prompt students against context-conditioned teachers as its core recipe, which is why P4 reads as a control rather than a discovery.
reviews.strongest_objection: The seed budget is allocated in inverse proportion to novelty. The only confirmatory, adequately powered comparison (3 seeds, all three sets, MDE ~4 net) is k=1 vs k=7 memory-free — i.e. exactly the claim 2608.12218 already established, ported to trajectories. Every claim that would make this a paper rather than a replication runs on the 2-seed exploratory ladder at a stated noise floor of ~±8 net: P2 asks for equivalence of DEC-7 to k=0 within 0.25 x Gate-0 gain (~3 net) with a CI more than twice that margin — an equivalence test that structurally cannot pass, and the brief's own rules forbid reading that failure as a null; P6 asks that RATE-3 sit strictly between two arms separated by less than the CI; and P4 asks for a monotonicity verdict over four teacher arms. Compounding this, P4 is close to definitional in the direction it predicts and under-identified in the direction it forbids: a student whose prompt is empty at training time has no context to become reliant on, so the mechanism 2608.12218 names (context lowers the loss the weights must close) is absent by construction, and 'non-decreasing' confirms nothing; if instead the teacher ladder declines at k_t=7, the proposal reads that as 'the effect is in the information, not the prompt', but the privilege-illusion literature — OP2SD arXiv:2608.09228 (verified), DAPD 2608.01735, DOPD 2606.30626 — already predicts a decline from off-support teacher targets a student cannot match. Two mechanisms, one observable, no arm that separates them. Secondary but concrete: the headline is gated on Gate 0 (k=0 QLoRA student must show >=12 net/100 memory-free gain) while the proposal's own Related Work cites Experience Distillation 2607.21051 (verified) reporting direct SFT retaining 3.8% of the in-context gain — on the measured +27/+32 here that is roughly +1 net. The proposal is therefore staking its primary experiment on an event its own literature review expects to fail, with amendment A1 changing the claim's scope if it does.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-allocate power to the novel claims: 3 seeds on DEC-7 vs k=7 (P2) and on the teacher-ladder endpoints (k_t=7 vs P-CD0), paid for by cutting k=3, RATE-3, or the self-rollout ladder — a smaller study that resolves the placement claim beats a 14-arm study that resolves only the replication. (2) Disambiguate P4 by adding the OP2SD-style shuffled-memory teacher at k_t=7 and reporting the teacher's own memory-conditioned accuracy and the student-teacher KL alongside student accuracy, so a teacher-side decline can be attributed to privilege illusion rather than to 'the information'; without this arm P4 cannot discriminate its own two readings. (3) Run Gate 0 first and report the k=0 QLoRA memory-free number as a standalone result before committing the ladder; if it lands near 3.8% retention, pre-commit to the context-distillation-target pool as the primary rather than as amendment A1. (4) Cost the evaluation grid honestly (see feasibility) and state which cells are actually funded. (5) Sharpen the decoy: other-type ALFWorld trajectories share action syntax and navigation subroutines, so DEC is a relevance-destroyed but not information-free control; report the measured delta-NLL of the decoy block and pre-register that P2's equivalence claim is void unless it is within noise of zero, otherwise DEC-7 is a low-dose arm and cannot separate 'abundance' from 'long prefix'.
reviews.missing_baseline: Each trained student evaluated at its OWN training dose (the k_train-matched deployment cell). The abstract opens on 'should an agent be fine-tuned with its retrieved experience in the prompt, so that training matches deployment' — but the test grid is absent / matched-k=3 / mismatched only, so the k=7 student is never run at k=7 and the deployment-matching hypothesis is never given its best case. A reviewer will note the paper argues against a policy it never actually deployed. Second omission: a dose-annealing arm (k decayed toward 0 over training), the obvious practical remedy and the one a reader will ask for the moment the monotone decrease is shown; RATE-3 varies the fraction of examples, not the schedule.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. Channel (a), the s2cli command, answered all six of my queries (every one returned s2=ok hf=ok); channel (b) WebSearch was unavailable this session (quota), so no section-level text was read and no abstract-level claim about a paper's internals could be checked. My queries: [1] 'training-time context dose reduces parametric encoding agent trajectories memory-free evaluation' --recent -> 12 hits, nothing on point (2606.04536 parametric memory for self-evolving agents, 2606.25342, 2604.20915 test-time training); [2] 'context distillation teacher-side privileged context versus student prompt context reliance dose ablation' --recent -> the privilege-illusion cluster: 2608.09228, 2608.01735, 2606.30626, 2607.05184, plus 2605.11458 (Adaptive Teacher Exposure for Self-Distillation: a learned schedule of teacher exposure — a teacher-side dose control, on reasoning not memory) and 2608.13040 (Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation, learns the privileged teaching context); none varies a retrieved-memory dose or contrasts student-side with teacher-side placement; [3] 'retrieval-augmented fine-tuning makes model dependent on retrieval degrades when retrieval removed at inference' (all years) -> only robustness-to-bad-retrieval work (2501.18365 RbFT, 2310.01558, 2410.05983, RA-DIT 2310.01352); nobody removes retrieval at test; [4] 'varying number of in-context demonstrations during supervised fine-tuning trades off memorization against context reliance' --recent -> 6 hits, top hit is 2608.12218 itself, plus 2503.09032 contextual fine-tuning; [5] 'internalizing retrieved experience into weights ALFWorld agent evaluated without memory at test time' --recent -> 12 memory-system papers (MemHarness 2607.28272, 2607.10608, 2605.30690, 2602.16313), none trains and then removes memory; [6] 'irrelevant long prefix control fine-tuning distinguishes context length effect from information content effect' --recent -> 5 hits, again 2608.12218 plus 2605.10828 (nonlinear effect of misleading long-context information, inference-time only). Verification of the IDs the novelty argument rests on: VERIFIED by `paper` — 2608.12218, 2607.21051, 2603.18272, 2606.01967 (title confirmed as 'Training Prompt Matters: State-Adaptive Optimization for Robust Fine-Tuning'), 2602.12275, 2606.29502, 2608.09228, 2607.29468; CONFIRMED to exist by appearing in my own search returns — 2608.05224, 2602.16313; NOT VERIFIED — 2605.09932, 2606.05684, 2604.05467, 2603.19313, 2601.05107, 2504.13145. Judging the proposal's own check: it is above average for this round — three queries with the channel status, explicit IDs for what came back, and honest negatives rather than a bare 'no prior work' — and I could not break it on the student-side axis. Its real gap is directional, not effortful: all three of its queries probe the student-side/abundance axis and none probes the teacher-side axis, so it never encountered the privileged-context distillation cluster my query [2] returned, including 2605.11458's teacher-exposure schedule and the OP2SD/DAPD/DOPD papers that supply the competing explanation for exactly the outcome P4 treats as decisive. A collision check that does not search the half of the design the paper's novelty depends on has established novelty for one arm only.
